title: Acute Corneal Hydrops: Clinical Crisis & Management Strategy
summary: Acute corneal hydrops is a sight-threatening complication of corneal ectasia where a rupture in Descemet's membrane allows aqueous humor to flood the corneal stroma. This masterclass poster details the pathophysiology, diagnostic nuances, and the shift from conservative to interventional management.

sections.title: Primary Etiologies
content: Keratoconus (Most common: usually stage 3-4 Amsler-Krumeich)
Pellucid Marginal Degeneration (PMD)
Keratoglobus (Higher risk due to generalized thinning)
Post-LASIK Ectasia
Vernal Keratoconjunctivitis (Associated with vigorous eye rubbing)

sections.title: Pathophysiological Sequence
content: 1. Progressive corneal thinning and mechanical stress
2. Rupture of Descemet's Membrane (DM)
3. Influx of Aqueous Humor into the corneal stroma
4. Massive stromal edema and epithelial bullae formation
5. Endothelial migration to bridge the DM gap

sections.title: Clinical Presentation (Symptoms)
content: Sudden, painless (initially) or painful drop in vision
Severe photophobia and epiphora
A visible 'white spot' or clouding on the eye
Foreign body sensation due to epithelial bullae
Blepharospasm

sections.title: Slit-Lamp Examination Findings
content: Localized or generalized corneal edema (ground-glass appearance)
Large stromal fluid clefts (intrastromal cysts)
Epithelial bullae (risk of rupture/infection)
Retracted DM scrolls (visible at the edges of the break)
Conjunctival hyperemia (ciliary flush)
Pseudopseudophakia appearance (extreme corneal convexity)

rows: Mid-dilated pupil, high IOP, shallow AC
Vertical DM breaks (Haab striae), history of birth trauma
Bilateral, guttae, central edema, slow onset

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Imaging
content: Anterior Segment OCT (AS-OCT): GOLD STANDARD to visualize DM break size and intrastromal clefts.
Pachymetry: Will show massive increase (often >1000 microns).
Slit-lamp Photography: For monitoring resolution progress.
Seidel's Test: Usually negative (the rupture is internal, not a full-thickness perforation).

sections.title: First-Line Medical Management
content: Hypertonic Saline (5% NaCl drops/ointment): Reduces epithelial edema (Muro 128).
Cycloplegics (Atropine 1% or Cyclopentolate): For ciliary spasm pain.
Topical NSAIDs/Steroids: To control secondary inflammation (use with caution).
Bandage Contact Lens (BCL): If epithelial bullae are causing significant pain.
Aqueous Suppressants: If IOP is elevated or to reduce pressure on the DM break.

sections.title: Surgical Intervention: Gas Tamponade
content: 1. Topical or peribulbar anesthesia in a sterile setting.
2. Paracentesis at the limbus.
3. Injection of Iso-expansile gas (SF6 20% or C3F8 14%).
4. Position the patient supine to allow the bubble to tamponade the DM break.
5. Monitor IOP closely for 24-48 hours (risk of pupillary block).
6. Gas facilitates faster endothelial migration and DM apposition.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Worry
content: Secondary Microbial Keratitis (Infection of bullae)
Full-thickness corneal perforation (rare)
Neovascularization of the cornea (high risk for future graft failure)
Persistent Flat Anterior Chamber after gas injection
Uncontrolled IOP (Pupillary block glaucoma)

content.explanation: H: Hypertonics, Y: Yield to time (often self-resolves), D: Descemet's repair, R: Rubbing cessation, O: OCT monitoring, P: Pain control, S: Surgical gas (SF6/C3F8).

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Evidence
sections.content: Basu et al. (2014) demonstrated that intracameral C3F8 reduces resolution time from ~100 days to ~20 days. Grewal et al. highlighted the utility of AS-OCT in identifying the exact location of DM scrolls, which determines the success rate of gas tamponade. Recent studies suggest pre-emptive cross-linking (CXL) in the fellow eye is vital as rubbing behavior is often bilateral.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls (Fellow Level)
content: The 'Silver Lining': Hydrops often leads to significant apical scarring and flattening, which can actually make contact lens fitting easier after resolution.
Wait before Grafting: Never perform PKP/DALK in the acute phase; wait at least 3-6 months for edema to clear and inflammation to subside.
The DM Break size: If the DM break is >1.5mm on OCT, medical management alone will take significantly longer; prioritize gas.
Steroid use: Use only mild steroids (Fluorometholone) to prevent slowing of endothelial migration while controlling discomfort.
Pediatric Alert: Children with Down Syndrome and VKC are high-risk; they require aggressive counseling against eye rubbing and early CXL.
